messages.author: 3c4d8081ca34423b
messages.subject: CX context dependent graphs
parts:
Hi all,

My all analysis will be CG context dependent. Starting from the basic histograms, I was not able to plot separate graphs with titles, for example %CHG methylation. I extracted each CX context by awk from Bismart Cytosine Report and assigned each context as separate samples under treatment 0.

From previous entries, I wanted to plot my own histograms.

Codes:

file.list = list("CysRep1.CG_report.txt", "CysRep1.CHG_report.txt", "CysRep1.CHH_report.txt")
sample.ids = list("CG","CHG","CHH")
myobjDB = methRead(location = file.list, sample.id = sample.ids, assembly = "mtr4", dbtype = NA, treatment =c(0,0,0), pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport", mincov = 10)

meth_histogram <- function(x, ...) {
 
  hist(myobjDB[[2]]$numCs/myobjDB[[2]]$coverage,
       main= "Histogram of % CHG methylation",
       xlab = "% methylation per base",
       col = "palevioletred")
}

Above histogram works, but coverage histogram does not work.

Code:

meth_coverage <- function(x, ...) {
 
  hist(myobjDB[[1]]$coverage,
       main= "Histogram of % CG methylation",
       xlab = "% methylation per base",
       col = "palevioletred")
}

Is there a way to make things easier for me? Honestly, it would be perfect if I was able to easily customize my plots.

Best,

Asuman

messages.author: 3c4d8081ca34423b
messages.subject: Re: CX context dependent graphs
parts:
In the coverage function, please ignore labelling. The problem is in the plot itself.

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: CX context dependent graphs
parts:
Hi Asuman,

If you do want to use your own plotting functions it might be best if you extract the underlying data from the methylDB object first using the getData() function. But if you want to use methylKit plotting functions, you should create one object for each context, meaning running methRead for each of your input files and adjusting the context argument accordingly.

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex,

Many thankss!!

I assigned sample id Rep1 to three context dependent objects in my first replicate, and revised my object like this:

myobjDB_CG = methRead(location = "CysRep1.CG_report.txt",
                      sample.id = "Rep1", assembly = "mtr4",
                      context = "CpG",
                      pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport",
                      dbtype = "tabix", mincov = 10)

In other contexts only object name, context and input file are different. I believe I can continue like that.

Best,
Asuman
